question: What is Frontman?
reply: Frontman is an AI agent that lives inside your app, not your editor. It plugs into your framework, giving anyone on your team a chat interface alongside a live view of your app. Describe what you want to change, and the agent makes it happen — outputting real code your team can review and merge.

question: How is this different from Cursor or Claude Code?
reply: Cursor and Claude Code work at the file level — they read your code but don't understand your running application. Frontman is wired into your app's runtime. It sees your component tree, routes, server logs, query performance, and everything happening live. That deep context means better results, faster. In our tests, it resolves changes 50% faster than Claude Code on the same tasks.

question: Who is Frontman built for?
reply: Designers, product managers, and other semi-technical people on engineering teams who need to make changes — from tweaking copy and structure, to exploring entirely new feature ideas. Engineers also benefit from the richer context and faster iteration loop compared to terminal-based tools.

question: Is it open source?
reply: Yes. Frontman is fully open source and runs locally on your machine.

question: What can I actually do with it?
reply: Implement a design change from a Figma mockup. Explore a new feature idea end to end. Tweak page structure or copy. Fix styling issues. Anything involving your frontend and fullstack application — described in natural language, executed as real code.

question: What does the interface look like?
reply: Navigate to localhost/frontman in your browser. You get a chat interface on the left and a live view of your app on the right. No terminal, no IDE — just a conversation with an agent that understands your entire system.

question: Isn't it dangerous to let non-engineers change code?
reply: Frontman runs in development only — never in production. Every change produces a standard code diff that goes through your team's normal review process. Nothing gets merged without an engineer approving it.

question: Which frameworks are supported?
reply: We're starting with Next.js, with more frameworks coming soon. Frontman integrates at the framework level as middleware, turning your app into an MCP server that exposes both client-side and server-side context to the agent.

question: How does it get context about my app?
reply: When you install Frontman, a lightweight middleware hooks into your framework. It exposes tools to the agent via MCP — client-side tools (component tree, performance, logs, click targets) and server-side tools (routes, server logs, query timing, compiled modules). Your app essentially becomes an MCP server that the agent can query in real time.
